subject: Clarify LOL cap vs prepaid refund + wind-down assistance

Subject: MSA + Order form redlines — liability cap and refund treatment

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. We reviewed and have a couple of material concerns before procurement will proceed:

- Limitation of Liability: our legal team wants the LOL cap to cover meaningful recovery for customer harm. The current 1x monthly fees is insufficient; can we discuss increasing this or adding carve-outs?
- Prepaid fees / termination refund: we prepaid for a 12-month term on the order form. The MSA currently limits refunds on termination for convenience — please confirm what Acme would receive if we terminate early.
- Wind-down assistance: we need clarity on what Redwood will provide (data export, KV cache handoff, short-term support). The SOW is vague.

Attached are our redlines (MSA_Redline_v3.docx) and the signed order stub. Can you confirm Redwood’s position this week? We’re hoping to close by Dec 10.

Best,
Amy Chen
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

Amy — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround.

High level: Redwood understands the concern and we want a practical compromise that preserves our SLAs and predictable economics. I’m looping in our legal lead (Monica) and sales ops (Rishi) so we can respond with specific redline language. A few clarifying asks up front:

- How much is the prepaid amount (you referenced 12 months) — absolute $ figure helps us propose a proportional cap.
- Is Acme willing to accept a cap tied to a lookback (e.g., fees paid in prior 12 months) vs. a fixed multiple?

Proposed approach from my side: offer a cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) 3x monthly recurring fees, carve out willful misconduct and gross negligence, and provide defined \"wind-down assistance\" limited in time and scope (e.g., up to 10 business days of hands-on assistance + data export). We will confirm with legal and get you a redline tomorrow.

Can we set up a quick 20m call Wed at 10am PT if that helps?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales—Enterprise, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Acme redline — cap vs prepaid refund + wind-down scope (need sign-off)

Team — forwarding Acme’s redlines. Key negotiation points:

1) LOL cap: Acme pushing for a higher cap than our proposed 1x MRR. They want something meaningful; they may insist on a multiple of ARR or the full 12 months prepaid.
2) Prepaid refund: Order shows 12 months prepaid; procurement expects refund pro rata on termination for convenience. We historically limit refunds to unused subscription period but cap damages. Need to be explicit.
3) Wind-down: Acme requests defined assistance (data export + short-term engineering help). This increases our delivery risk and cost.

My suggested positions (for discussion):
- Cap = greater of (last 12 months fees) or (3x monthly recurring fee).
- Exclusions: unlimited for willful misconduct / gross negligence; no liability for consequential/incidental damages.
- Refund: pro-rata refund for unused prepaid period on termination for convenience, subject to a processing fee (or offset for work performed).
- Wind-down: offer up to 10 business days of \"reasonable\" assistance; additional days to be billable at published rates.

Monica — can you confirm risk tolerance and proposed redline language? Rishi — cost model for 10 days of handover (eng hours) so we can put a $ estimate in offer. Lauren — if this escalates to legal procurement, we may need a commercial concession (credit or onboarding support).

Thanks — Jonas
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme redline — cap vs prepaid refund + wind-down scope (need sign-off)

Quick legal take and a draft we can propose to Acme:

Risk tolerance: moderate. Customer is strategic and mid-enterprise; prefer to avoid prolonged back-and-forth. That said, unlimited exposure is unacceptable.

Suggested contract language (high level summary we can deliver as a redline):
- Limitation of Liability: Except for either (i) Redwood’s willful misconduct or (ii) Redwood’s gross negligence, Redwood’s aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (A) the fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim, or (B) three (3) times the average monthly fees paid by Customer under the applicable Order Form during the 12 months preceding the claim.
- Consequential Damages: Exclude consequential, incidental, and punitive damages, except to the extent prohibited by applicable law.
- Refund on Termination for Convenience: Customer shall be entitled to a pro rata refund of any prepaid, unused subscription fees for the remaining term as of the effective date of termination, less any non-cancelable third-party costs and reasonable wind-down costs documented by Redwood.
- Wind-down Assistance: Redwood will provide up to ten (10) business days of reasonable wind-down assistance (data export, standard configuration handoff, and knowledge transfer). Additional assistance will be billed at Redwood’s then-current professional services rates.

We can provide a marked-up MSA (Redwood_Legal_Suggested_LoL_Text.docx). Two negotiation levers: (1) adjust the multiplier (2x v 3x) and (2) increase/reduce wind-down days. If sales wants to be more generous (e.g., 15 days or 3x multiplier) we should document the commercial trade (credit, free onboarding, or onboarding support).

Rishi — can you produce an estimate for 10 business days of handover (eng + solutions) and an incremental cost for 15 days? I’ll prep the redline file once we have the numbers.

— Monica
attachments: Redwood_Legal_Suggested_LoL_Text.docx

Subject: Re: MSA + Order form redlines — liability cap and refund treatment

Jonas / Monica — thanks for the quick internal review and the suggested language. Acme’s position after internal review:

- Acceptable cap: the greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) three (3) times the average monthly fees (this mirrors Redwood’s proposal).
- Consequential damages: mutual waiver of consequential/incidental damages is acceptable.
- Refund: Acme requires pro rata refund of unused prepaid subscription fees on termination for convenience without an opaque processing offset; we can accept reasonable administrative deductions, but not a generalized "wind-down cost" that is unbounded. Please provide an estimated dollar amount for the 10-day assistance so procurement can evaluate.
- Wind-down assistance: Acme would accept up to ten (10) business days of reasonable assistance; additional days billable. We request the assistance include export of customer data in commonly-used formats and a single knowledge-transfer session with Eng/CS.

If you can provide the estimated cost and a clean redline with the proposed text, Acme’s GC will move to approval. Aim to have that to us by EOD Mon so we can finalize by Dec 10.

Best,
Natalie Green
Counsel, Densley & Partners (external counsel for Acme)
